name: mdxmini
desc: Plays music in X68000 MDX chiptune format
why: Plays X68000 MDX chiptune files, a door into a obscure Japanese retro sound format and its hardware era.

brief.what_it_is: mdxmini is a C library with a small API for playing back MDX chiptune files made for the X68000 home computer. A caller opens an MDX file (plus an optional directory of .pdx sample files), reads metadata such as title, length in seconds, and track count, then calls mdx_calc_sample repeatedly to render raw PCM audio into a buffer at a chosen sample rate. Each call can also report the note or sample index active on each channel, which is useful for visualizations. The README's Shift-JIS note means titles come back in that encoding.
brief.why_it_exists: The README presents it as a way to play the large MDX archive of FM-sound-era music from the X68000, whose 8-channel YM2151 and PCM chip gave it strong music support. The Credits section traces it from the original X68000 MXDRV player through Daisuke Nagano's Unix mdxplay to BouKiCHi's library.
brief.how_it_works: The caller initialises a t_mdxmini struct with mdx_open, sets the output rate with mdx_set_rate, and then loops on mdx_calc_sample to fill a 16-bit buffer. mdx_calc_sample returns 0 at the final frame of the song. mdx_get_current_notes fills an array with per-channel values: channels 0 to 7 are FM notes (0 is the lowest C), and channels 8 to 15 are PCM sample indices. The README does not say how the chip output is generated internally.
brief.install_notes: The README gives no build, install, or dependency steps. The API is documented in the mdxmini.h header, and the README's C sample shows the call sequence. The Homebrew formula provides an executable named mdxplay, but the README does not describe how that binary works or how to run it. Some songs need a directory of .pdx sample files passed as path_to_samples, which can be NULL.
brief.standout: It is a reusable playback library rather than only a player, and it exposes live per-channel note data for visualizations. Its downstream uses include an Android player and the Modizer music-module player, so the same core runs on mobile and desktop.
brief.status: unknown. The README has no dates or version notes. The GitHub releases page has no releases. The README names Misty De Meo as current maintainer, but I could not check recent commits.
brief.caveats: The README covers only the library API and gives no build instructions, supported platforms, or licence. The mdxplay executable in the Homebrew formula is not described in the README, so I could not confirm its options or behaviour. Songs that use PCM samples need the matching .pdx files on disk. Titles are Shift-JIS encoded and need decoding for display. The README's example playback-position arithmetic looks convoluted, so treat the sample loop as illustrative rather than exact.
quotes: mdxmini is a C library with a simple API which can play back MDX chiptunes from the X68000 home computer.
The X68000 was, for its time, an advanced 16-bit computer with excellent multimedia support; its 8-channel YM2151 sound chip and 1-channel PCM chip gave it excellent music support.
Detailed API documentation is available in the mdxmini.h header file, but the following sample program shows how to use mdxmini to open a file, extract some metadata, and play back music
